---
title: "Two anchors, one prior"
subtitle: "Catalog C-09"
description: "From TSMM to the Dual-Anchor prior at J = 50 in four linked views: the prior on alpha, the count K_50, the weights with the .40 trigger, and the chance two units share a cluster."
toc: false
---

The Dual-Anchor refinement changes one Gamma prior, and every view of the model moves with
it. Press the button to go from TSMM, which anchors the count only, to the paper's
Dual-Anchor choice at lambda = .30, which also anchors the weights.

```{=html}
<div id="w-rec" class="dpx-host column-page"></div>
<script src="../../js/vendor/d3.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/vendor/plot.min.js"></script>
<script src="../../js/bundles/reconcile-dashboard.js"></script>
<script>
  (function () {
    var q = new URLSearchParams(location.search), spec = {};
    ["a", "b"].forEach(function (k) { var v = q.get(k); if (v !== null && v !== "" && isFinite(+v)) spec[k] = +v; });
    if (q.get("preset")) spec.preset = q.get("preset");
    window.__dpxRec = DPX["reconcile-dashboard"].mountWidget(document.getElementById("w-rec"), spec);
  })();
</script>
```

- **The count gives a little.** E K_50 moves from the target 5.00 to 5.88: about one more
  expected cluster.
- **The weights give a lot.** Pr(W_SB > .5) falls from .497 to .398, just under the .40
  trigger; the chance that two random units share a cluster falls from .518 to .439.
- **What changed in alpha.** Its mean rises from 1.31 to 1.63 and its spread shrinks (CV .84
  to .66). In restaurant terms, a newcomer is a little more willing to open a new table, so
  the first table dominates less often.

Use the a and b sliders to see how sensitive each view is near the Dual-Anchor choice. The
full lambda frontier is on [the Dual-Anchor page](dual-anchor.qmd), and the whole workflow is
on [the J = 50 worked example](worked-example-j50.qmd).

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Endpoints: data/precomputed/worked_example_j50.json (replication package, CC BY 4.0). Every
value is recomputed with dp-core at each frame. With reduced motion the change is immediate.
:::

(for example `?preset=da`).
